report.source_text: Initial laboratory investigations showed a decreased serum albumin level of 33.5 g/L then 28.2 g/l (normal rage: 35–50 g/L) and proteinuria of 4.5 g/day (urinary total volume 1000 mL). Microscopic examination of the urine showed microscopic hematuria (80–100 cells/HPF) and leukocyturia (50,000/mL). Electrophoresis of serum proteins showed a polyclonal peak in gamma globulins at 33.6 g/L. Serum creatinine was 58 μmol/L. The patient's blood test results showed a leukocyte count of 4900/mm3, with 1100/mm3 being lymphocytes, hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, and a platelet count of 178,000/mm3. The patient's antibody test showed a positive result with a titer of 1:1800 and homogenous pattern. Additionally, the patient tested positive for anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies with a titer of 1:40, and for anti-Sm (+ +), anti-RNP (+ +), and anti-SSA antibodies (+). The complement C3 and C4 levels were reduced to 42 mg/L (normal range: 81–157 mg/dL) and 7 mg/dL (normal range: 13–39 mg/dL), respectively, while CH50 was 9.5 U/mL (normal range: 31.7–95 U/mL). The results for Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody, Coombs' test, antiphospholipid antibody, serum cryoglobulins, serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis, and anti-PLA2R antibody were all negative.

report.source_text: A renal biopsy was performed. Light microscopy showed that 8/34 glomeruli were sclerotic and the rest showed segmental mesangial deposits and infiltration of neutrophils, but no mesangial cell or stromal proliferation. The glomerular basement membrane was diffusely thickened with segmental spikes. The renal interstitium contained some inflammatory infiltrates, and the tubules showed small focal atrophy and scattered proteinaceous and red blood cell casts. There was intimal fibrous proliferation and sclerosis of small arteries. Congo red stain for amyloid was negative. Direct immunofluorescence showed full-house staining along the mesangium and the capillary loops with subepithelial immune deposits of IgG (3 +), IgA (+), IgM (1 +), C3 (2 +), C1q (1 +), fibrinogen (2 +), albumin (−), kappa (2 +), lambda (3 +).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with Class V (Membranous) Lupus Nephritis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old North African female presented with 1 month of lower extremity edema, photosensitive skin lesions (neck, face, chest), asthenia, 3 kg weight loss, and amenorrhea for 1 year. Initial urinalysis showed 2+ proteinuria and 1+ hematuria. Physical examination revealed firm curved erythematous patches on the neck, face, and chest with moderate bilateral lower limb edema. Admission laboratory workup revealed positive ANA (1:1800, homogenous pattern), positive anti-dsDNA (1:40), positive anti-Sm, anti-RNP, and anti-SSA antibodies, reduced complement C3 (42 mg/L) and C4 (7 mg/dL), heavy proteinuria (4.5 g/day), and microscopic hematuria (80-100 cells/HPF). Renal biopsy demonstrated diffusely thickened glomerular basement membrane with segmental spikes, segmental mesangial deposits, and full-house immunofluorescence staining pattern (IgG 3+, IgA +, IgM 1+, C3 2+, C1q 1+, fibrinogen 2+, kappa 2+, lambda 3+), consistent with Class V (membranous) lupus nephritis. Laboratory findings also showed leukopenia (4900/mm³), lymphopenia (1100/mm³), and decreased serum albumin (28.2 g/L). The patient met six EULAR/ACR 2019 SLE classification criteria with a total score of 31.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Positive ANA with high titer (1:1800) and homogenous pattern
Positive anti-dsDNA antibodies (1:40) and anti-Sm antibodies
Reduced complement C3 (42 mg/L) and C4 (7 mg/dL)
Photosensitive skin lesions (firm curved erythematous patches on neck, face, and chest)
Glomerular proteinuria (4.5 g/day) with microscopic hematuria (80-100 cells/HPF)
Renal biopsy with diffusely thickened GBM with segmental spikes and full-house immunofluorescence pattern (IgG 3+, C3 2+, C1q 1+, fibrinogen 2+)

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Full-house immunofluorescence pattern with C1q and fibrinogen deposition is characteristic of lupus nephritis, not primary membranous nephropathy. Positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, and anti-Sm antibodies are specific for SLE.
Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) was negative (E001). Positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm antibodies are inconsistent with ANCA-associated disease.
Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody was negative (E001). Full-house immunofluorescence pattern is inconsistent with anti-GBM disease.
Antiphospholipid antibody was negative (E001). Clinical presentation and serologic findings are consistent with SLE rather than isolated APS.
Serum cryoglobulins were negative (E001). Full-house immunofluorescence pattern and positive anti-dsDNA/anti-Sm are inconsistent with cryoglobulinemia.

remaining_uncertainties: Explicit documentation of EULAR/ACR 2019 classification criteria scoring (which six criteria were met and how the total score of 31 was calculated)
Explicit WHO/ISN-RPS classification statement confirming Class V (membranous) lupus nephritis (inferred from histopathologic findings of thickened GBM with spikes and subepithelial deposits)
Exact timing of renal biopsy relative to initial presentation (documented as 'on admission' but specific date not provided)
Treatment initiated (immunosuppressive therapy) and clinical response/outcome
